selection_exposure: Source MotifGNN/GitHub and DOI found exploratorily; 87.46MB archive obtained before prereg; zip inventory, source code and CSV headers read; NO rows of observed relationships and NO outcome/statistical summaries yet. Data-source discovery not preregistered.

A.question: In the independent real dating interaction graph SSJY shared by MotifGNN authors, is mutual directed action more frequent than a degree-constrained directed configuration null, and can the dataset identify exposure, rejection and relationships? This tests only graph reciprocity, not ESBM causal mechanism.
A.unit: Unique directed user-ID pair with at least one click/msg in log; platform users in original archive; not platform-wide eligible dyads or observed exposure sets.
A.population: Self-selected SSJY dating-platform actors with logged actions; no known sampling weights or population generalizability; 2020-era Asian platform uncertain geography.
A.estimand: Directed arc reciprocation fraction: count unique directed i→j with observed j→i divided by unique directed arcs excluding self links. Comparison expected under exact event in/out degree stub permutation.
A.true_outcome: Presence of reverse recorded click/msg action
A.proxy_limit: Reverse edge is NOT app match, explicit mutual swipe, meeting, relationship, durable union or evidence of rejection; nonedge is NOT no/decline.
A.harm: No individual identifiers, profile text, coordinates, emails, or raw rows in GitHub; no pkl unpickling, no credentialed scripts or remote database calls.

B.H0: Reciprocal arcs explained by observed user event outdegree and indegree under uniformly paired directed stubs; observed rate compatible with 30 permutations.
B.H1: Observed reciprocal arc proportion exceeds degree-conditioned stub-null by more than all 30 simulated null replicates.
B.Halt: Interaction network strongly assortative or group restricted, old actions mixed click/msg; stub-null ignores social/algorithmic exposure and action differences. Even statistical excess is NOT uniquely due to mutual desire and cannot identify ESBM mechanisms.

C.data_zip: Public file linked from original authors official GitHub README https://github.com/RManLuo/MotifGNN (master); Google Drive https://drive.google.com/file/d/1u-59m0u5-pcF4TCN6zjGLICWFdQteCUG/view?usp=sharing
C.primary_test: Compute unique nonself directed arc reciprocation; degree-preserving event-stub randomization using 30 PCG64 seeded permutations of target endpoints across observed original events, preserve exact event in/out counts before dedup; drop self loops; collapse duplicates; compare 30 null rates to observed.
C.stats: report observed reciprocation, observed number unique reciprocal pairs; null mean/min/max and empirical upper-tail Monte Carlo p=(1+count(null>=observed))/(B+1), B=30. If none exceed, report bound p=1/31≈0.0323, not p=0.
C.multiplicity: single primary stat (arc reciprocation); descriptive secondary file types, duplicate events, self loops, role mixing; no extra hypothesis selection.
controls: R0 null shuffles all target stubs preserving in/out event degrees; controls activity and popularity, but no gender preference, selection of shown profiles, platform rules or timeline; not a competent causal ESBM baseline.
If graph cannot expose directed distinct actions, STOP claim; if date absent, no longitudinal inference.

D.procedure: Parse zipped relations.csv in RAM with pandas; never unpickle enc_feature_dict.pkl, never run bundled source scripts or connect to author Neo4j (hardcoded credentials found in archive). Map user IDs to local numeric codes; pack pairs into uint64, unique arcs, compare reverse arc via numpy searchsorted; 30 random degree-preserving target permutations. Preserve complete author archive hash and script SHA, run once; save only aggregate JSON and QA, no source rows.
D.environment: Python 3, pandas/numpy; bound memory; clean_clone_NOT_VERIFIED; code artifact to be committed before run
D.privacy: Aggregate outputs only, no sample rows, no deanonymization, no credentials.

adversarial: No exposure denominator and no explicit negative responses
No timestamps means cannot identify temporal influence/after rejection/relationship duration
Edges reused for generated train/test labels: possible label leakage when features use full graph; not automatically claim paper model leaked
No source dataset license file in official GitHub root found; public sharing allows inspection but redistributing data or derived identifiable rows not licensed
Degree-only null ignores sex mixing/community constraints, any surplus is not evidence of causal reciprocal preference
Duplicate interactions can produce excessive stub-degree null variability, report both event and unique arcs
Action msg vs click not necessarily like/dislike

G.independent_replication: No independent study of ESBM. One source distinct from Mixmosa, Columbia, Rios, Hitsch, pairfam; 30 permutations are a null test not external replication. No 2/3.

H.action: append SOURCE/UPDATES qualitative after results, explicit NO_CHANGE_WITH_REASON when not identifying a scientific claim; no numeric Bayesian priors.

I.CT2_after: set after experimental audit; cannot rise merely by using a large unrelated graph
I.new_grade: 0/3 unless new, unique, independently replicated evidence with novel claim (not anticipated).

J.decision: If legally accessible source real and original graph analyses succeed: one valid N81 A–J, leave N82–N86 untouched and STOP_R5 if lacks exposure/negative/temporal; if no schema or legitimate rights to analyze, classify plan only and keep 6. Never claim match/duration from mutual click/msg.

DRIFT: D0.7, same matching domain with independent directed interaction graph, narrower outcome proxy

rights.read: Author publicly shared file via official GitHub without access barrier; no site terms explicitly granting redistribution and no LICENSE in GitHub root; only local inspect aggregate analysis, if rights unresolved don't republish original rows; license and privacy remain caveats.
